ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed shareholders, managers, and beneficiaries against PEP databases, OFAC SDN List, UN Sanctions Lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Luxembourg domestic sanctions screening through CSSF/KYC systems. Unless the customer is a structurally trivial corporate vehicle, enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons. Transaction monitoring must cover unusual or suspicious activity according to CSSF circulars and the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory documentation and corporate names may be filed in French, German, or Luxembourgish; names derived from Latin script are accepted, but if the desired name originates from a non-Latin alphabet, a certified transliteration into Latin script and translation into French must be provided. The name must comply with Luxembourg linguistic rules and must not be confused with an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a name rejection by the Luxembourg Business Registers or the RCS, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar within fifteen working days of the rejection notice. The appeal must be lodged by counsel and set out the reasons why the proposed name is not prohibited, misleading, or confusingly similar to an existing name. If the administrative appeal is rejected, judicial appeal may be filed before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within one month of the appellate decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not fully permissible for a Luxembourg SARL in the substance-driven model. A registered office in Luxembourg is mandatory, but the use of a licensed domiciliation agent (société de domiciliation) is acceptable provided that the agent is supervised by the CSSF or the Ministry of Justice and that actual management functions and accounting records are maintained in Luxembourg. A pure virtual address without any artificial corporate substance is not permitted and would violate Luxembourg commercial, tax, and AML/CFT rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For this standard-profile low-risk design subscription agency, the quantified risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Luxembourg tax administration, CSSF, or municipal authorities is estimated at 15% within the first three years when the registered office is solely domiciled with a professional agent; the risk rises substantively if the company fails to maintain adequate substance or if the business model becomes inconsistent with the registered premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended by the Law of 10 August 2016 and the Law of 23 September 2020; SARL provisions at Articles 710-1 to 710-20; registration and legal publication framework under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and Annual Accounts (loi du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés ainsi que la comptabilité et les comptes annuels des entreprises).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de commerce et des sociétés - RCS), operated by the Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA - AEDT); electronic filing via the eJustice portal (www.ejustice.etat.lu).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte de constitution) executed before a Luxembourg notary and filed electronically with the RCS; a private deed under Article 710-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915 is legally permissible for a SARL, but the notarial form is the market standard and supports fast-track one-day incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital of EUR 12,000 must be fully paid up at incorporation (Article 710-5 of the Law of 10 August 1915). Cash contributions are deposited with an eligible EU/EEA credit institution in a blocked account (compte bloqué) opened in the name of the SARL in formation; the bank issues a blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the Luxembourg notary. The funds are released only after RCS registration. In-kind contributions are permitted, must be fully paid in, and must be described in the notarial deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Sole Shareholder subscribes and fully pays the share capital of EUR 12,000, acknowledges the bank blocked-funds certificate, and approves the Articles of Association of the SARL. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at [Insert Address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, subject to acceptance by the RCS. RESOLVED, that [Full Name] is appointed as sole Manager (Gérant) with plenary powers of management and representation, including authority to open bank accounts, sign subscription contracts, and engage staff. RESOLVED, that the Manager, together with the notary, is mandated to complete RCS registration, publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés, VAT registration and all ancillary formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) - name check desk and eJustice portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a list of one to five proposed corporate names to the RCS for a name availability assessment (certificat de non-confusion). Verify that the name does not conflict with existing RCS registrations, does not create a likelihood of confusion in the Luxembourg market, and complies with public policy. The RCS issues a confirmation of availability for a limited reservation window, which the notary attaches to the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Corporate object and business activity description (UI/UX design subscription services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS flags a conflict or requires modification, promptly submit amended name options and re-run the clearance. There is no formal appeal against a name observation; the standard procedural cure is selection of a compliant name before notarization.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg maintains a split administration. Direct taxes: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), official portal impotsdirects.public.lu. Indirect taxation (VAT, registration duties): Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), functional portal guichet.public.lu and MyGuichet.lu (secure e-filing 'espace sécurisé'). The single company taxpayer identification number (matricule national) is allocated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) upon RCS incorporation; EU-wide VIES data exchange is managed by the ACD/AEDT under Regulation (EU) No 904/2010.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the SARL before a Luxembourg notary and file for registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the LBR; the registered legal entity automatically receives the 15-digit national identification number (matricule national), which is the operative corporate TIN for all Luxembourg tax filings. Step 2 - For VAT, file VAT Form 31 (Déclaration d'assujettissement) with the AEDT, after which a 'LU' + 8-digit VAT identification number is issued; non-established foreign entities must file Form 31 and appoint a local VAT representative (représentant responsable) before making any taxable supply. Step 3 - Activate the MyGuichet.lu secure professional eSpace for electronic submission of CIT/ICC/IFL returns, monthly VAT returns, EC Sales Lists, and OSS returns. Step 4 - Register any payroll employees with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for social security withholding. Step 5 - For export/refund workflows, open a Luxembourg bank account (payments via Stripe Billing/Wise must be traceable to the Luxembourg balance sheet) and register for the electronic customs filing platform to link export declarations with AEDT zero-rating substantiation files.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Luxembourg SARL is a fully taxable resident company: corporate income tax (IRC) at 17%, municipal business tax (ICC) at the communal rate (approx. 6.75% in Luxembourg City), solidarity surcharge 7% on IRC, and net wealth tax (IFL) at 0.5% on net assets exceeding EUR 500,000 (0.25% above EUR 500 million). Territorial scope is worldwide income taxation of residents; a broad participation exemption, SOPARFI holding regime, and 80% IP box deduction are available. Pass-through treatment is not available; Tax_Exempt_Zone status does not exist in Luxembourg for general trading entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not offer a US-style check-the-box election; relevant statutory elections for structuring are: (a) VAT grouping election for Luxembourg-resident group companies (Article 61a of the 1979 VAT Law); (b) small-enterprise exemption waiver permitting voluntary VAT registration below the EUR 35,000 threshold; (c) IP box election for 80% exempt qualifying IP income (Article 50bis LIR); and (d) tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) election for 95%+ Luxembourg-resident group chains. EU hybrid mismatch neutralizing rules (ATAD, implemented by the Law of 25 March 2020) automatically override elective outcomes that create double non-taxation, deduction-without-inclusion, or double-deduction scenarios.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA), governed by the Luxembourg Law of 12 February 1979 implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Luxembourg-established businesses: no mandatory VAT registration threshold; small enterprises with annual taxable turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000 (exclusive of VAT) are exempt from VAT compliance but may elect to register. Non-established foreign suppliers: mandatory Luxembourg VAT registration from the first euro of taxable supplies made in Luxembourg; digital/e-commerce services supplied to Luxembourg consumers require quarterly OSS filing (no threshold) once the EUR 10,000 cross-border distance-sales threshold is exceeded in the EU.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based tax clearance, or digital stamping regime exists as of the 2025 tax period. Mandatory domestic B2B e-invoicing will phase in under the Law of 15 March 2023 (Bill 7318): issuers with more than 300,000 invoices per year from 1 September 2026, remaining taxpayers and mediums by 1 September 2028. The mandated transport standard is Peppol (UBL 3.0 / CII); invoices must be exchanged electronically via certified Peppol access points. Until the mandate, e-invoicing is voluntary and must respect Article 75 VAT Law content rules (sequential number, issuer/customer VAT IDs, date, description, quantity, price, VAT rate, reverse-charge mention). Cross-border B2B design-subscription supplies must be reported in the monthly VAT return and the VIES/EC Sales List. OSS/IOSS digital service portals require authenticated MyGuichet.lu API integration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Luxembourg SARL supplying UI/UX design subscriptions (ISIC 7410) claims VAT relief as follows: (1) physical exports of design deliverables to non-EU territories: 0% tax with proof of dispatch out of the EU by customs export declaration; (2) intra-EU B2B supplies of services (the core subscription business): the general B2B place-of-supply rule (Article 38 VAT Law/Article 44 EU VAT Directive) locates the supply where the business customer is established - Luxembourg VAT is therefore not charged (zero-rated/reverse-charge in the customer state), provided the customer's valid EU VAT identification number is stated on the invoice and substantiated via VIES; (3) services to non-EU B2B clients fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (no Luxembourg VAT), and (4) B2C supplies to EU consumers are taxable in Luxembourg at 17% (place of supply at the supplier's establishment), unless effectively an electronically supplied service subject to the EU consumer-state rule. The zero-rate is conditional on contemporaneous written evidence of customer identity, VAT number, contract, and payment trail.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ED-5 filed via the Luxembourg customs Single Window)
Bill of Lading / CMR or e-CMR / Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Commercial invoice and signed subscription/design services contract
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds
VIES validation printout of the EU customer's VAT number
EUR.1 movement certificate or origin invoice declaration where preferential origin is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg imposes no exchange-control repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is the prudential export-proceeds standard applied by the AEDT and customs authorities when assessing zero-rating files. Fraudulent export zero-rating or false reverse-charge assertions trigger: arrears interest of 0.8% per month (9.6% per annum) on the uncollected VAT; administrative fines under Article 53 of the VAT Law ranging from EUR 10 to EUR 10,000 per infringement; and, for intentional tax fraud (Article 98 VAT Law), fines of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of one month to five years. The AEDT cross-checks export declarations (ECS/ICS, SAD), bank data received via DAC7/DAC8, and VIES sales-listings; retrospective clawbacks cover the standard 5-year assessment limitation period, extended to 10 years for fraud or failure to file. Directors of the SARL are jointly and severally liable for fraudulent VAT schemes and export-transaction misstatements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); supervisory and regulatory interface for exchange control matters is shared with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which licenses credit institutions and enforces AML/KYC rules on payment flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the EU Treaty regime of fully liberalised capital movements (TFEU Article 63). Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible in EUR; there are no exchange control permits, no approval thresholds, and no restrictions on foreign ownership of a SARL. Profit remittance faces no FX or administrative hurdle, but outbound dividends are subject to a statutory 15% Luxembourg withholding tax, reducible to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU parents and to treaty rates (e.g., 5% or 0% under double tax treaties depending on the shareholder jurisdiction) for non-EU parents. Payments for services (royalties, design fees, contractor fees) are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax and may be remitted freely, subject only to the bank's standard documentary review and sanctions filtering.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion of foreign currency receipts into EUR. There is no legal timeline for repatriation of export income; the entity's only obligation is indirect statistical reporting: the resident bank acts as the BCL's reporting agent for balance of payments (ITRS) data and will request a transaction purpose code for cross-border cash movements. Design subscription revenues collected in USD, GBP, or other currencies may be held offshore to the extent permitted by bank terms, yet treasury risk policy should favour conversion within 5-10 business days to EUR unless a documented hedging strategy exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as a supplementary collection-and-disbursement rail, LOW as the primary treasury or capital-custody rail. Wise (Wise Europe S.A., licensed as an electronic money institution by the National Bank of Belgium with EU passport) and Stripe (Stripe Payments U.C., authorised by the Central Bank of Ireland) are legally usable for inbound subscription collections and outbound contractor payments in EUR, USD, and GBP. However, EMIs are not credit institutions under Luxembourg law: they cannot hold statutory subscribed capital in a blocked compte bloqué, cannot offer ISDA-derivative or FX hedging documentation, may cap high-value cross-border disbursements, and do not assume the role of BCL statistical reporter. All treasury balances above the equivalent of EUR 10,000 should be held at a CSSF-regulated bank; EMIs should receive at most two days of receivables float before a sweep.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance requirement is the default for opening the capital escrow compte bloqué at most Luxembourg incumbent banks: at least one manager and all signatories holding 25% or more must attend an in-person compliance interview at the bank's head office, bringing original passports, the notarised deed of incorporation, and proof of registered office. Remote opening is permissible only for the operational account of a Low-risk B2B design-subscription SARL where (i) the manager holds an eIDAS-qualified digital identity, (ii) all UBO documentation is apostilled and translated, and (iii) the bank's compliance committee approves a videoconference KYC session (CSSF AML Circular 20/07 risk-based approach). In practice, the first onboarding is faster with a physical visit to a Luxembourg City branch; a remote videoconference is accepted at BIL and BGL BNP Paribas for the operational account but not for the escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered or non-transparent UBO chain: shareholders include a venture fund or holding entity in the U.S., UAE, or Asia with nominees, or the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing has not been completed, causing the bank to reject the file.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a consolidated chain-of-title package: certified share registers, apostilled board resolutions and articles for every intermediate holding entity, the accepted RBE confirmation for LuSARL, a notarised UBO declaration identifying all natural persons above 25%, certificates of good standing from each jurisdiction, and a written AML counsel opinion confirming that no nominee arrangements exist and that the design-subscription activity is fully transparent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-flow opacity from aggregated payment providers: 90% of the SARL's revenue arrives through Stripe and Wise as non-bank settled card and wallet traffic, lacking counterparty names in the bank's transaction monitoring system.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver six months of Stripe Billing and Wise Business transaction exports with line-item customer identifiers; an updated customer register naming the three largest subscribers (with KYB/company extracts where relevant); a sample Design-As-A-Service subscription agreement; a policies-and-procedures memo describing the ISIC 7410 / NAICS 541430 commercial model, payment terms, and churn; and a commitment letter that all new clients with annual B2B payments above threshold will be verified before onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Subscribed capital injection is flagged as unusual: the EUR 12,500 minimum subscribed capital arrives from a third-country parent through an intermediate correspondent in a risky jurisdiction, triggering unexplained-wealth and source-of-funds queries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble the original SWIFT MT103 confirming the remitter matches the notarial deed; the authenticated deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) showing subscription of shares; the parent shareholder's 12-month bank statements; a source-of-wealth declaration signed by the contributing shareholder; an updated balance-sheet extract of the parent; and evidence that the identity of the remitter aligns with the beneficial owner recorded in the RBE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursement pattern to freelance production hubs in Ukraine, India, and Vietnam for UI/UX development labour is interpreted by automated monitoring as payable-round-tripping or inadvertent sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide per-contractor KYB/KYC cards (passport copy, business register extract, address proof), signed subcontracting agreements containing AML and sanctions clauses, itemised invoices linked to specific design deliverables, a recurring payment calendar, a confirmation that no end-client is located in sanctioned jurisdictions, and the board-approved outsourcing register demonstrating legitimate design-asset production.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographies in the client base: B2B subscription clients in the United States and Gulf states whose identification at onboarding is considered incomplete for a distance-services company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a sanction-screening protocol and a client-tiering matrix demonstrating that each non-EEA subscriber is a vetted legal entity with evidence of the underlying commercial purpose; include entity registration extracts, billing addresses, and bank account verification for the three largest non-EEA clients; demonstrate that automatic blocks are enforced for sanctioned territories; and produce a monthly export showing that all subscription contracts are digital design engagements with identifiable invoice references.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of audited/annually approved financial statements (comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg business register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end (calendar-year SARL: by 31 July); AGM approval must occur within 6 months of year-end (by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court fines of EUR 500–5,000 for late deposit; forced filing ordered by the Commercial Court; failure to file for more than 12 months triggers the administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) procedure under the law of 24 August 2022, leading to dissolution and transfer of assets to the State.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual corporate tax filing: corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg direct tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year (calendar-year SARL: FY 2024 return due by 31 December 2025); extensions available on reasoned request via the eCDF e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Estimated assessment (taxation d'office) by the tax office; late-filing surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax; monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%; criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 for willful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO (RBE) register confirmation, including updates triggered by share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation within one month of the anniversary of RBE registration; any change in beneficial ownership (e.g., transfer reaching or exiting the >25% threshold) must be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties for non-compliance: imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years and/or fines up to EUR 1,250,000 for legal persons; suspension of RBE certificates/good-standing extracts; adverse AML due-diligence impact.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' ordinary general meeting approving annual accounts, profit appropriation, and discharge of managers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate act recorded in the statutory minute book; evidenced copy accompanies the RCS filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end (calendar-year SARL: by 30 June); yearly recurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered extraordinary meeting at the company's expense on petition of any interested person; unresolved approval blocks the statutory RCS deposit and exposes managers to civil liability for resulting damages.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a réviseur d'entreprises agréé only if the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, average headcount above 50; a court or a shareholder minority representing the statutory threshold may also require an audit; below thresholds the SARL is audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts (Plan Comptable Normalisé; simplified formats available for small/micro entities); IFRS as adopted by the EU optionally permitted for individual annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial owners (any natural person holding or controlling more than 25% of share capital or voting rights, or otherwise exercising control) are declared to the RBE; any share transfer or direct/indirect ownership change requiring an RBE update is filed within 30 days of the triggering event and the entity re-declares its UBO data annually within one month of the anniversary of its RBE registration, even if the data remain unchanged.

Register of share transfers and capital operations
Minute book containing general meeting resolutions and manager decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,600–US$5,400 per year (EUR 1,500–5,000) for commercial domiciliation, registered office, and corporate administration; higher if accounting/substance support is included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,400–US$16,200 (EUR 5,000–15,000) for a statutory audit if thresholds are exceeded; EUR 0 when the audit exemption applies and no shareholder-requested audit is made

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (IRC) + 7% solidarity surcharge on IRC (effective IRC 18.19%) + municipal business tax of 6.75% in Luxembourg City => combined statutory burden ~24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% profit deduction for qualifying intellectual property (Art. 50bis LIR) covering software copyrights and product-design rights; 44% super-deduction for R&D expenditure (EUR 50m ceiling); 8%-13% investment tax credit; notional interest deduction (NID) for new equity; participation exemption at 100% for dividends and capital gains from >=10% subsidiaries held >=12 months.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit); post-change-of-ownership annual set-off capped by Art. 114(4) LIR when majority ownership and activity are structurally altered
